content: Perylene, also known as perilene, is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C20H12. It appears as a brown solid. This compound, or its derivatives, may exhibit carcinogenic properties and is classified as a hazardous pollutant. In the field of cell membrane cytochemistry, perylene is utilized as a fluorescent lipid probe. Perylene exhibits blue fluorescence and is employed as a blue-emitting dopant material in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), either in its pure form or as a substituted derivative. Additionally, perylene can function as an organic photoconductor. The molecular structure of perylene consists of two naphthalene units connected by a carbon-carbon bond at the 1 and 8 positions of each naphthalene molecule. All carbon atoms in the perylene molecule are sp² hybridized. When representing the structure of perylene, it is critical not to depict the central ring as a fifth benzene ring. Doing so would result in two carbon atoms becoming sp³ hybridized, which would disrupt the aromaticity of the molecule and compromise its ability to fluoresce. The structure of perylene has been extensively analyzed using X-ray crystallography.
